findings.title: Unused-resource recommendations overstate the observed history as 30 days
findings.what: Each detector consumes hygiene findings but filters only on resource type and windowCount, discarding the findings' short-retention hedge. It then unconditionally states that the resource was unused “in the last 30 days.” With less than 30 days of retained sessions, the evidence proves only the shorter observed interval, so the recommendation's historical claim is not reproducible from its input.
findings.fix: Preserve the hygiene hedge or retained-window duration when constructing each recommendation. When history is shorter than 30 days, use an explicitly bounded phrase such as “unused in the available history as of <date>” (ideally including the observed duration); reserve “last 30 days” for inputs that actually cover that interval.
findings.acceptance: Add deterministic cases for all four detectors with less than 30 days of retained history and assert that neither title nor detail claims 30 days, that the output includes an as-of date or observed-window provenance, and that a dataset covering at least 30 days still emits the existing 30-day wording.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read at the immutable baseline confirmed that every cited detector passes sessions and now into computeConfigHygiene, then retains only resourceType/windowCount and emits unconditional 30-day wording. Directly related baseline code was checked solely to verify behavior: computeConfigHygiene calculates a window-shorter-than-threshold hedge from the oldest retained session, proving that the necessary contrary signal exists but these four dispatched files discard it. Existing short-window fixtures use timestamps only 100,000,000 ms apart (about 1.16 days), confirming the condition is reproducible; those comparison tests are not listed as defective files.
